issues.detail: Both locales inherit the source opening claim that one line is read, followed by a claim that the whole file is returned. This is not introduced by translation. Replace the opening with reading file contents (subject to the configured size limit); do not describe a line-based operation. The preserved callback example need not change. The newer promise overload is an omitted source capability, not a translation error.

resolution.detail: Independently reread both revised summaries and the unchanged callback example. They now describe file contents subject to the configured size bound and no longer claim a one-line operation; the promise capability is not invented in this callback-focused text.

issues.detail: The conceptual success/failure summary is followed by the accurate source warning “Not yet implemented!” in details. All maintained database definitions still have null rollback hooks, so the current implementation returns 0 for valid supported-backend handles. This is inherited, not a translation defect. Clarify in the summary that the described operation is currently unavailable; retain the warning and do not imply working rollback support.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now separate the historical 1/0 convention from current null backend rollback hooks, return 0 only for an authorized valid handle, and state invalid-handle failure. Existing not-implemented details remain accurate.

issues.detail: The source and both locales list errors twice and omit objects in the prose key list, although their example includes objects. Replace only the repeated final errors with objects in both locale prose lists. Do not add cost or worth merely from the upstream Markdown: the maintained implementation emits exactly moves, errors, heart_beats, array_size, objects. The author note cites a driver document that is itself stale.

resolution.detail: Both prose lists now match the five keys actually emitted by get_info. Existing mapping examples and definitions remain unchanged; stale Markdown cost/worth keys were not added.

issues.detail: The source 暂停 and English suspend imply execution can resume at this point. error() raises a runtime error and unwinds/halts the current execution; it does not pause a resumable thread. Change the two locale descriptions to raising the error and stopping/unwinding the current execution, with catch handling as appropriate. Preserve err, the * prefix and debug-log description.

resolution.detail: Both revised summaries describe runtime-error unwinding to catch/recovery rather than resumable suspension. Debug tracing is qualified by error handling; err and the literal * prefix remain intact.

issues.detail: The inherited signature example shows string args, but the later prose calls args an array exclusively. The maintained efun accepts string or string-array arguments. Clarify the natural-language args description as accepting either form without rewriting the preserved source signature/example. Also have the summary refer to the details callback prototype rather than suggesting the read callback receives only a data string: details already correctly includes int fd first.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now allow string or string-array args and identify the read callback fd before data. Existing signature example and complete callback prototypes remain unchanged. Original text references now point to the locked fixture after structural migration.

issues.detail: Both locales retain the source contradiction that directory-listing paths end in / but give /adm as an example. The maintained implementation returns the matching single entry when a nonempty final path component exists, and enumerates the directory for a trailing slash. Correct the natural-language example to /adm/ in a separately authorized factual correction; this is inherited source text, not a translation-introduced code change.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now distinguish /adm/ directory listing from the preserved /adm entry-match example. Existing backtick tokens, returned tuple and -1/-2 semantics are unchanged; the new quoted example is plain prose.

issues.detail: The source header annotation says LT_YEAR >= 1900 while the prose and English translation say strictly greater than 1900. Neither locale should strengthen that to >1900. More fundamentally, maintained code returns tm_year + 1900 with no driver-enforced 1900 lower bound; timestamp support is delegated to the OS. Describe LT_YEAR as the calendar year and qualify the quoted historical header claim rather than asserting a mandatory lower bound. The historical v2017/v2019 details were translated faithfully; their platform/date limits were not runtime-validated in this review.

resolution.detail: Both revised summaries call LT_YEAR the calendar year and explicitly qualify the unchanged historical >=1900 header comment using tm_year+1900 and host-system limits. Historical v2017/v2019 details remain faithful source content and have not been runtime-validated.

issues.detail: The final preserved example refers to class exaample, while the class declaration is example. This typo predates translation and is deliberately preserved in both locales under the example/identifier preservation rule. Record for a source-example correction; do not treat it as a new translation defect or silently change the copied identifier in this review.
issues.reference: config/efun-docs/docs/new.json:summary (class declaration and final initialization example)

resolution.detail: Both locales now use class example in the final unfenced initialization, matching the declaration. Root authorized this one identifier typo correction. User literals, the preceding example body and the remaining final example text are unchanged; there is no inline/fenced markup to exempt.

issues.detail: The English source and both locales refer to “applies below”, but the field contains no list below. Remove the dangling below/下面 reference or link to an authoritative apply list in a separate source-text correction. The cache invalidation behavior and blue-to-red example are otherwise preserved.

resolution.detail: Both summaries remove only the dangling below/下面 apply-list reference, without inventing a missing apply list or changing invalidation behavior or the blue-to-red example.

issues.detail: The source and both locale prose/table descriptions for a string argument with omitted object mention only the current environment. Maintained code first searches this_object() inventory, then the environment object itself via id(), then its inventory. Include that search order in both prose and the repeated usage row. The unusual object-argument return of the parent object is confirmed by source and must remain unchanged.

resolution.detail: Both opening prose and repeated usage row now include current inventory, environment object, then environment inventory in the source implementation order. The independently confirmed object-argument parent return behavior remains unchanged.

issues.detail: The Chinese locale retains the ambiguous/incorrect source clause “如果对象没有投影或被投影返回 0”; it can say a shadowed object returns 0. English correctly states neither shadows another object nor is shadowed. Align Chinese with that conjunction: return 0 when the object has neither relationship (or is unavailable), otherwise remove its relationship and return 1. The implementation unlinks the specified object from the shadow chain; do not expand this into destructing the shadow.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now describe unlinking the specified object from its shadow chain and use the correct neither-shadows-nor-is-shadowed condition for 0. They preserve non-destruction semantics and return 1 for actual unlinking.

issues.detail: The source and both locales say the left side. Maintained rtrim removes trailing/right-end characters. Change left/左侧 to trailing/末尾 in both locale summaries. The fact this was inherited and noted by the author does not make the shipped two-language claim correct.

resolution.detail: Both revised summaries now say trailing/right end. The maintained trim implementation confirms the direction; existing historical availability text is unchanged.

issues.detail: The input is consistently str except for the unchanged-original-string sentence, which says sr in the source and English locale. This inherited prose identifier typo should refer to str. Do not alter the signature, bit position, limit, growth rule or six-bit encoding.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now use str consistently. The author declaration precisely permits the single protected token replacement `sr` -> `str`; no bit position, numeric limit, growth rule or six-bit encoding statement changed.

issues.detail: The Chinese translation “返回参数 f 的正弦值，单位为弧度” attaches radians to the sine result, which is dimensionless. The original English means the input f is measured in radians. Use “返回参数 f 的正弦值，其中 f 以弧度为单位” (retaining the original quote style around f). The English locale already preserves the correct source meaning.

resolution.detail: The Chinese summary now explicitly assigns radians to input f. English is unchanged; no unit is assigned to the dimensionless sine result.

issues.detail: The source and both locales inherit the nonexistent mode spelling STEAM and incorrectly restrict listening to STEAM/MUD. Correct to STREAM and describe supported stream modes, including MUD, STREAM (also normalized STREAM_BINARY), STREAM_TLS and STREAM_TLS_BINARY; datagram modes cannot listen. Note that bind is required before listening. For a usable TLS server, configure the certificate/key before listening; the code warns but does not reject immediately when they are absent, so avoid claiming a mandatory immediate error. Do not copy the upstream Markdown mode list blindly because it omits normalized STREAM_BINARY.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now include STREAM_BINARY normalization, supported stream/TLS modes, bind-before-listen and datagram exclusion. Missing TLS cert/key is accurately described as warning rather than immediate rejection; callback prototype and return/error details remain unchanged.

issues.detail: The opening sentence in both locales inherits printf behavior: output to the current player. sprintf returns the formatted string, as this document details already states. Change only the opening behavior to formatting and returning a string; keep the controls, flags, widths, precision descriptions and preserved printf(%%) example.

resolution.detail: Both revised openings now say format and return a string, consistent with the unchanged details. Independently checked all subsequent controls, flags, widths, precision and examples remain unchanged.

issues.detail: Both locales retain the source milliseconds unit. time() returns seconds since the epoch. Replace milliseconds/毫秒 with seconds/秒 in the two summaries, preserving the epoch and Beijing-time equivalence. This is an inherited source error that still needs correction in the shipped locale data.

resolution.detail: Both summaries now use seconds, preserving the epoch and Beijing-time equivalence. This agrees with the maintained time documentation and implementation.
